cancho.title: A leaked file, refused by name

steps.note: It opens a file and never closes it. The compiler refuses:
The refusal is data an agent can match on:
One added line fixes it, and the program may now run:
steps.cmd: diff leak.cho fixed.cho; cancho build fixed.cho --std -o notes && ./notes

steps.note: What may it do? The types say:
steps.out:
performs
    fs_read("/tmp")
    io_write
never touches
    the network
    the heap
    the command line
    signals
    other programs
    foreign code

cancho-ui.title: A component that asks for the clock

steps.note: Delete `requires Clock;` and the compiler refuses:
steps.out:
error[capability-missing] at clock_bad.cui:15:21: component `Clock` performs `clock.now` which requires the `Clock` capability, but `requires Clock` is not declared
exit 1

steps.note: With the declaration it is accepted:
Ask what it may reach, as data:
steps.cmd: cancho-ui inspect effects clock.cui Clock | grep '"capability"'

trail:door-sensors.title: A day of door sensors, in cancho
trail:door-sensors.summary: Readings arrive over MQTT, are kept in a cache, and are summarised by table. Every stage is a cancho binary except three small Python stand-ins.
trail:door-sensors.source: A recorded run of the real tools, replayed; the sensors, the bridge and the MQTT client are Python stand-ins (cancho-mqtt-client is on the map as design).

steps.note: A broker, and a cache that speaks Redis. Both cancho.
The cache answers, and any Redis client will do.
Three door sensors publish a day of readings; a small bridge (Python, a stand-in for cancho-mqtt-client, which is still on paper) files them.
The cache holds the latest reading per sensor.
steps.cmd: for s in hall kitchen garage; do echo "$s $(redis-cli -p 16379 GET latest:$s)"; done

steps.note: And every reading is a row for table.
Ask table for the average. It refuses, by rule, and the hint says how to say what the column is.
steps.out: {"ok":false,"command":"table","schema":"table.v2","error":{"code":"INVALID_ARGS","rule":"agg.bad-spec","message":"an item of --agg is not count, sum:COL, min:COL, max:COL, mean:COL or distinct:COL, or its :int, :dec(S) or @N is not one that item takes","hint":"--agg count,sum:bytes,max:bytes,distinct:status; a mean of an integer column needs its scale, mean:bytes@2; a decimal column is declared sum:price:dec(2)","repair":null,"detail":{"item":1,"agg":"count,mean:celsius"}},"errors":[{"code":"INVALID_ARGS","rule":"agg.bad-spec","message":"an item of --agg is not count, sum:COL, min:COL, max:COL, mean:COL or distinct:COL, or its :int, :dec(S) or @N is not one that item takes","hint":"--agg count,sum:bytes,max:bytes,distinct:status; a mean of an integer column needs its scale, mean:bytes@2; a decimal column is declared sum:price:dec(2)","repair":null,"detail":{"item":1,"agg":"count,mean:celsius"}}],"meta":{"version":"0.3.0"}}
